Job Title: Senior Product Manager

Location: Remote, USA

 
 

About the Company

Wheel is evolving the traditional care ecosystem by equipping the nation's most innovative companies with a premier platform to deliver high-quality virtual care at scale. We offer proven strategies and cutting-edge technologies to foster consumer engagement, build brand loyalty, and maximize return on investment. Wheel solutions include configurable virtual care programs, an intuitive consumer interface, and access to a nationwide network of board-certified clinicians. Discover how Wheel is transforming the future of healthcare by visiting www.wheel.com.

 
 

About the Role

A prescription only helps a patient once it's covered, filled, and affordable. For the companies that run virtual care programs on Wheel, getting that right is the difference between a program that grows and one that stalls on denials, pharmacy errors, and manual follow-up. This role owns that layer.

As a Sr. Product Manager, you'll own the product roadmap for how patients get their medications covered, filled, and paid for across Wheel's enterprise partners. Your scope covers prior authorization, eligibility and benefits checks, pharmacy connectivity and prescription routing, and patient payments.

You bring deep insurance and pharmacy expertise. You know how payers and PBMs make coverage decisions, how pharmacies adjudicate and fill prescriptions, and why claims, PAs, and fills fail. You know how commercial and government programs differ.

Much of this work is still highly manual, and you'll define and build AI and automation into these workflows to drive measurable business value. For patients, that means getting on the medication they need faster, with fewer denials and dead ends. For Wheel and our partners, it means programs that scale efficiently, with nurses focused on clinical judgment instead of paperwork.

You'll work in a small, senior squad with Engineering, partnering closely with Clinical, Operations, Legal, Compliance, and Account Management. This is a hands-on role: you'll go deep on payer and pharmacy workflows, integration specs, and data.

 
 

What You'll Do (Job Duties/Responsibilities)

Prior Authorization & Insurance

  • Own Wheel's prior authorization capability end to end, from coverage and formulary signals at prescribing through submission, payer response, appeal, and resolution, across electronic, portal, and fax channels

  • Design workflows that hold up across commercial and government programs, keeping programs cleanly separated where their rules differ

  • Use denial and payer-response data to find root causes of failed authorizations and turn them into product fixes

  • Identify where AI can improve efficiency and patient experience while reducing manual effort across PA, eligibility, and pharmacy workflows, validate those opportunities with Operations, and turn the strongest ones into shipped capabilities

Pharmacy & Payments

  • Own pharmacy connectivity and prescription routing across retail, mail-order, and specialty pharmacy partners, including selection, transmission, status, and exception handling

  • Define requirements for new pharmacy integrations and build state- and partner-level fulfillment rules into the platform

  • Diagnose where prescriptions fail between prescriber and pharmacy (for example, identifier mismatches, non-covered NDCs, rejected claims) and automate detection and resolution of recurring failures

  • Own patient payment capabilities, including checkout, recurring billing, consent, cancellation, and refunds, and drive transparency so patients know what they'll pay before they commit

Roadmap, Measurement & Delivery

  • Own the squad's quarterly roadmap and backlog, sequencing partner commitments, payer and pharmacy requirements, and regulatory changes into shippable plans

  • Define success metrics for each capability (for example, approval rate, time to therapy, fill rate, nurse time per case) and report results after launch

  • Define how each AI capability is evaluated before and after launch, including accuracy, escalation, and failure modes, and implement guardrails with Clinical, Legal, and Compliance, bringing them in early rather than at the end

  • Serve as the squad's go-to expert on payer, PBM, and pharmacy rules, and give Account Management and Clinical clear input on what a given program can support

  • Write capability briefs, PRDs, and acceptance criteria engineers can build from, and manage product-level relationships with external partners (ePA and e-prescribing networks, pharmacies, payment processors)

What Success Looks Like

  • First 90 days: You own the PA, pharmacy, and payments roadmap and backlog, have mapped where coverage and fills fail today, and have shipped your first improvements.

  • First 6 months: You've identified and prioritized where AI fits across PA and pharmacy workflows, and you have the first AI-assisted capability scoped with clear evaluation metrics and in build.

  • First 12 months: You've expanded the payer and pharmacy coverage Wheel can support for partners, and you're a trusted voice on what's feasible across product, clinical, and partner teams.

 

Who You Are (Job Qualifications)

Required

  • 5+ years of product management experience, including owning a product area end to end

  • Deep insurance and pharmacy domain expertise, whether gained in product or in operations at a PBM, payer, pharmacy or pharmacy services company, e-prescribing or ePA vendor, or revenue cycle organization

  • Hands-on knowledge of prior authorization, eligibility and benefits, formulary management, and pharmacy claims adjudication, including why each fails

  • A track record of shipping AI-powered or automation features into production, and the ability to explain how you scoped, evaluated, and monitored them

  • A builder's way of working: you prototype concepts and ship working tools yourself (for example, with AI coding tools, scripts, or SQL) to test ideas and automate workflows before handing them off to Engineering

Strongly Preferred

  • Working knowledge of pharmacy operations across retail, mail-order, and specialty settings, and of state pharmacy regulations

  • Experience with both commercial insurance and Medicare Part D (Medicaid a plus)

  • Familiarity with NCPDP SCRIPT/ePA and telecommunication standards, X12 270/271, NDCs, and NCPDP ID/NPI identifiers

  • Experience building integration-heavy products with external partner APIs in a B2B2C or platform model

Nice to Have

  • Pharmacy credential or clinical background (for example, PharmD or CPhT)

  • Experience shipping payments or subscription products, including consent, renewal, and cancellation compliance

  • Telehealth or direct-to-consumer care experience

How You Work

  • You map end-to-end workflows across clinical, operational, payer, and pharmacy steps and see where they break

  • You're technically fluent: comfortable reading API docs and tracing behavior in logs or queries

  • You define metrics precisely and separate measured results from reported ones

  • You use AI tools daily to speed up discovery, specs, and analysis

  • You communicate clearly with engineers, operators, and executives, and you make scope calls you can defend

 

Salary and Perks

Pay Range: $170,600-$220,000 plus equity

Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including, but not limited to scope and responsibilities of the role, the selected candidate’s work experience, education and training, the work location as well as market and business considerations.

Wheel is unable to consider sponsoring a new qualified applicant for employment authorization for this position.

As an employee of Wheel, you’ll enjoy our Total Rewards Program to help secure your financial future and preserve your health and well-being, including:

  • Medical, Dental and Vision

  • Ancillary: Life, Short and Long Term Disability

  • 401K match

  • Flexible PTO

  • Parental Leave

  • Stock options

  • Additional programs and perks

Wheel is committed to equal employment opportunities for all team members. Every decision we make regarding employment is solely based on merit, competence, and performance. We are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills.

Research shows that underrepresented groups typically apply only if they meet 100% of the criteria listed. At Wheel, we encourage women, people of color, and LGBTQ+ job seekers to apply for positions even if they don’t check every box for the role.
